{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Workflow 17 with one more scene: on the line Out walks a fox with a silver cane, the fox from the song walks in and stands on her desk while she keeps singing. An Add person scene brings in anyone (or anything) from one picture.

 Steps

  1. 1. Load your song and set where the singing begins (drag on the waveform).
  2. 2. In H3 Timeline, make one scene per part of the song: its length, a few words about what happens, and a picture. Scene 1's picture is the first frame; a New look moves her to a new place; an Add person picture brings someone in (scene 3 here).
  3. 3. Seed: F (fixed) gives the same video every Run, R (random) a new take.
  4. Press Run.

 The pictures

  • One person, the same clothes, a new place in each picture. The demo's 4 pictures were made with Nano Banana in Google Flow: the kitchen one first, then the other 3 FROM it (the kitchen picture added as a reference), so she stays the same person. The same sweater in every picture makes her read as the same person at once.
  • Portrait (9:16), chest up, the face big, so the singing mouth reads clearly.
  • A new place changes the WHOLE picture, so each change is a short see-through crossfade, like a dissolve between shots in a music video.
  • Use clean, full-size pictures, never a frame grabbed from a video: in the tests a video frame made the rest of the video softer.
  • The one who walks in: one clean picture of them, whole, on a plain background (the demo fox: Nano Banana, a fox in a tweed coat with a silver cane, standing on a grey studio floor). Set the scene's role to Add person. Write where they come from and what they do: walks in from the right side of the frame right away, at the very start, and stops beside her desk. right away brings them in at the start of the scene.
  • How they leave: here the next scene moves her to the sofa (a New look picture of her alone), so the fox leaves with that change of place. If the next scene stays in the same place, write their exit at the end of their own scene instead, or they fade out like a ghost.

 The song and the scene lengths

  • Give each scene one or two sung lines and put the cuts in the pauses between lines, so a change of place never lands in the middle of a word. The demo: 9 + 5.5 + 4.5 + 10 + 12 seconds = 41 seconds: the desk part of workflow 17 is split in two, and the fox's scene starts at 14.5 seconds.
  • To find the pauses, play the song and note where each line starts, or look for the quiet gaps in the Load Audio waveform.
  • The scenes set the length: the song is cut to their total. The demo song was made with Suno from two short verses with no chorus, so it sings from the first second.
  • A song with one clear lead voice works best.

 Good to know

  • Write what the person does in each scene, short and concrete, like sings at her desk, glances at the computer beside her and then back to the camera. The node puts your words into the tested Sing prompt for you.
  • Another seed gives another take: a different glance, smile or way of moving.
  • Bigger sizes: set the width and height in H3 Timeline (multiples of 32). Bigger is sharper and slower (see Run Times), and a scene drifts more often: H3 zooms into her face or changes the wall. In the tests 480 x 864 kept all 4 places; at 576 x 1024 one seed of two kept all 4 (the other turned the desk into a close-up); at 704 x 1280 both seeds drifted somewhere. So for a sharper video try 576 x 1024, check every scene and try another seed if one drifts. 864 x 1536 and bigger ran out of memory on a 24 GB graphics card. Sharper still: workflow 18 (clean cuts) kept all 4 places at 704 x 1280.
  • Up to 12 scenes. A 60-second video at 480 x 864 took about 5.5 minutes in the tests.
  • Keep a scene where someone joins at about 13 seconds or less. Whoever joins is the least predictable part: in some tests a person came in twice. Run again with another seed if that happens.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Nodes look different from the video

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed) - Holds the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA: 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Audio Pixaroma (1. your song) - Your song. Drag on the waveform (or type a Start) to begin where the singing begins. The scenes in H3 Timeline set how many seconds are used: the song is cut to their total.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • H3 Audio Sync Pixaroma (your song in the render) - Locks your REAL song into the render, so the mouth sings with the voice in it. The saved video carries exactly your song.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves, except H3 Timeline: there you set your scenes.

  • H3 Timeline Pixaroma (2. your scenes) - The whole video as scenes: each scene has its own length, its own words (what the person does) and, if it needs one, its own picture. Scene 1's picture is the first frame. A New look picture in a later scene moves the same person to a new place. Made in one Run, with no cuts.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Video Pixaroma (the singing video) - Saves the video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Singing with your song, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Video size (width x height)the 41-second demo song
480 x 864, the defaultabout 3.5 minutes
bigger sizessee workflow 17

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a smaller card

Start with the smallest size and 5 seconds. The Free VRAM node already hands memory back before the video decode. A clip that is too big for the card gets very slow long before it stops working.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
